PCA Biplot with Feature Selection

rna_biplot.Rd

Generates a PCA biplot using previously computed dimensionality reduction results, highlighting genes based on their contribution to principal components and/or association with a grouping variable.

Usage

rna_biplot(
  project,
  use_dimred = NULL,
  group_col = "Group",
  style = c("loading", "anova", "hybrid"),
  colors = NULL,
  n_genes = 10,
  genes = NULL,
  point_size = 2,
  save = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

project

rna_project object created by rna_project().

use_dimred

Optional dimred_object to use in rna_biplot.

group_col

Character. Column name in metadata used for grouping samples.

style

Character. Method used for gene selection. One of "loading", "anova", or "hybrid".

colors

Character. Optional point colors.

n_genes

Integer. Number of top genes to display when biplot_genes is not provided.

genes

Character vector. Optional vector of gene names to include. Overrides automatic selection.

point_size

Numeric. Size of sample points in the plot.

save

Logical. Whether to store results in the active rna_project.

verbose

Logical. Whether to print the plot.

Value

A list of class biplot_result containing:

  • biplot: list with selected genes, coordinates, scores, and PCs used.

  • plot: ggplot object of the biplot.

Details

The function supports three modes for gene selection:

  • loading: selects genes with highest contribution to selected PCs

  • anova: selects genes most associated with the grouping variable

  • hybrid: combines loading magnitude and ANOVA significance

Gene selection can be automatic (top-ranked) or user-defined.

The biplot is constructed from a previously computed PCA stored in rna_project. Gene vectors are scaled to match the PCA coordinate space.

In hybrid mode, both loading magnitude and ANOVA-derived significance are normalized to the range [0,1] before combination.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Standard PCA biplot
rna_biplot(project = my_project)

# PCA biplot with a specific gene set
rna_biplot(project = my_project,
           n_genes = 2,
           genes = c("IL6", "HSP70"))
} # }
